History of Present Illness:
73-year-old woman. One day of right upper abdominal pain with chills and two episodes of vomiting. No chest pain or dyspnea.

Physical Examination:
Focal right upper-quadrant tenderness and guarding; no costovertebral angle tenderness. Temperature 37.4 C; heart rate 106/min; BP 116/78 mmHg; respiratory rate 22/min; SpO2 97% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 15.1 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.9 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 276 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 138 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 4.1 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 117 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 40 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 64 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 51 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 101 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: stones, gallbladder wall 6 mm, pericholecystic fluid and focal sonographic tenderness; bile ducts not dilated.
